args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. A human approver approved the rollback. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying, and check why it was promoted even though the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Problem:** The latest deploy put v2.3.1 in every region (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The service was failing health checks there, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. A human approver signed off on the rollback, and all three regions now run v2.3.0. I checked the status afterwards: the service is healthy and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 as a SEV2 for checkout-api, and the on-call engineer has been paged. It says what failed, the rollback to v2.3.0, the results after it and what to do next.

v2.3.1 had already shown up as unhealthy in staging (as v2.3.1-rc) but was still promoted to production. I noted this in the incident so the team can look at why it got through, as well as finding the root cause before redeploying.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
